posts.title: Gonzo's revenge
posts.description: You talk about your news dumps. Here's a doozy, dropped at 3:00 on Black Friday afternoon to ensure minimum visibility: The City of Portland is going to pay former City Councilman Rene Gonzalez north of $100,000 to settle his federal lawsuit claiming that the city auditor violated his due process rights by pursuing him for campaign finance violations while other candidates were allowed to get away with similar misdeeds. Gonzalez had alleged that his top rivals in the 2024 mayoral race, Keith Wilson and Carmen Rubio, likely broke the same rule but weren’t investigated. The auditor’s office subsequently found that Wilson’s election campaign violated city campaign finance law by accepting some donations over the legal limit. The campaign was fined $526.... The city isn’t confident it would win in court against Gonzalez, according to city documents. posts.title: Bingo! Here's your news dump.
posts.description: As expected, it took until 5:22 p.m. on Thanksgiving Eve for the news to break , but the head of "Prosper Portland," Cornell Wesley, is " out of the office and not working while the matters raised in the Union’s recent letter are considered by the Board." The chair of that board, Gustavo Cruz, is being secretive about what exactly that means, but in the meantime, the economic development agency has a new acting head, Lisa M. Pettinati. Pettinati, a finance lawyer, has been at Prosper (formerly the Portland Development Commission) only about five months. Before that, she spent eight years or so as a deputy general counsel for the Oregon State Treasury. Previously she was assistant general counsel for the Overseas Private Investment Corporation (which eventually became the the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation).
